n: One of the tenderest chapters in the Bible. God speaks as a loving parent: “When Israel was a child, I loved him, and called My son out of Egypt.” Matthew sees this pattern fulfilled when the child Jesus returned from Egypt.

f.w: called my son out of Egypt
When Israel was a child, then I loved him

n: The more God (through His prophets) called them, the further they wandered—offering sacrifices to the Baals and burning incense to idols.

f.w: As they called them, so they went from them
f.g: The more they were called, the more they turned away.

f.w: Baalim

n: Like a parent teaching a toddler to walk, God held Ephraim by the arms—yet they never realized it was He who healed them.

f.w: I taught Ephraim also to go
they knew not that I healed them

n: God led them with gentle cords of human kindness and love. He was like someone who lifts a yoke off an animal’s neck and bends down to feed it. God’s leadership is loving, not harsh.

f.w: I drew them with cords of a man, with bands of love
I laid meat unto them
f.g: I bent down and fed them.

n: Because they refused to return to God, they will not go back to Egypt—instead Assyria will rule them.

f.w: the Assyrian shall be his king

n: War will rage through their cities and destroy them, because of their own schemes.

f.w: branches
f.g: Possibly “gate bars” or “boasting priests”; the Hebrew is uncertain.

n: God’s people are determined to turn away. They are called upward to the Most High, but none will lift Him up.

f.w: bent to backsliding

n: The emotional climax of Hosea: “How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over?” Admah and Zeboiim were destroyed with Sodom. God’s heart recoils; His compassion is stirred. Divine love wrestles with justice.

f.w: How shall I give thee up, Ephraim?
Admah
my repentings are kindled together
f.g: My compassion grows warm and tender.

n: God will not carry out His fierce anger or destroy Ephraim completely, “for I am God, and not man.” Human anger seeks revenge; God’s holiness includes mercy that endures.

f.w: for I am God, and not man
the Holy One in the midst of thee

n: A future gathering: they will follow the Lord, who roars like a lion to call His children home. They will come trembling from the west.

f.w: he shall roar like a lion
the children shall tremble from the west

n: They will come swiftly like birds from Egypt and doves from Assyria, and God will settle them in their homes—a promise of the gathering of Israel.

f.w: I will place them in their houses

n: Ephraim surrounds God with lies and deceit. Judah is described as still walking with God, though the Hebrew may mean Judah too is unruly; translations differ. (In many Bibles, this verse begins chapter 12.)

f.w: Judah yet ruleth with God
f.g: The Hebrew is unclear; some translations read “Judah still wanders from God.”
